title: Separation permanence for arbitrary algebraic stacks
statement: Work over a field $k$ [def-weil-field], with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], algebraic stacks [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and the $2$-fibre products of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Representable means representable by algebraic spaces. Properties of representable morphisms are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts. Let $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $g:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be morphisms of algebraic stacks. Separated means proper relative diagonal, with algebraic-space properness tested on scheme charts [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Then separated morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change and under composition. For representable maps the separated predicate agrees with the closed-immersion diagonal predicate on algebraic-space tests [def-weil-closed-immersion].

proof.text: First justify the algebraic-space tests of every relative diagonal used below. A scheme map $T\to\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A$ is a triple $(x_1,x_2,\alpha)$ with $\alpha:f(x_1)\simeq f(x_2)$. Its pullback of $\Delta_f$ is the sheaf of isomorphisms $\beta:x_1\simeq x_2$ satisfying $f(\beta)=\alpha$. Thus it is the sheaf fibre product $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal A,T}(x_1,x_2)\times_{\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal B,T}(f(x_1),f(x_2))}T$, with $T$ mapping by $\alpha$. Both Isom sheaves are algebraic spaces by the cited statement, and their fibre product is an algebraic space. This identification is on objects and arrows: a diagonal-lift triple is sent to the isomorphism between its two displayed identifications with $x_1,x_2$; conversely $\beta$ gives the lift $x_1$ with identifications $\mathrm{id},\beta$. The evident isomorphisms are inverse naturally. All stack products used here and below are algebraic by the algebraic-stack fibre-product lemma.

We spell out how the existing algebraic-space properness statements apply to representable stack maps. If $p:\mathcal U\to\mathcal V$ is representable and every scheme pullback is proper, then for any algebraic space $Z\to\mathcal V$ its pullback $U_Z\to Z$ is an algebraic-space map by the space-valued pullback lemma. Every scheme test $T\to Z$ of this map is the original test $\mathcal U\times_{\mathcal V}T\to T$ by associativity of triples. The arbitrary-scheme-test criterion therefore makes $U_Z\to Z$ proper. For composable representable proper maps, a scheme test of the composite factors through the algebraic space obtained by testing the second map; the first factor is proper by the preceding argument, the second by hypothesis, and algebraic-space proper composition applies. For any base change of a representable proper map, a scheme test is simply its original test by the composite map to $\mathcal V$, so is proper. Representability of these maps follows from the cited fibred-groupoid calculus. These arguments also show that properness is invariant under the canonical equivalences: their corresponding space tests are isomorphic over the test scheme.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal B'\to\mathcal B$ be arbitrary, put $\mathcal A'=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal B'$, and write $f':\mathcal A'\to\mathcal B'$. Identity (1) of the diagonal node identifies $\Delta_{f'}$ as the base change of $\Delta_f$ along $\mathcal A'\times_{\mathcal B'}\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A$. If $f$ is separated then $\Delta_f$ is proper. The representable base-change argument in step 2 makes $\Delta_{f'}$ proper, which is precisely separatedness of $f'$.

For separated $f,g$, factor the composite diagonal as $\mathcal A\xrightarrow{\Delta_f}\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal A$. On an object $a$ it gives $(a,a,\mathrm{id}_{gf(a)})$, so this composite is $\Delta_{gf}$. Identity (2), with $u=v=f$ and $h=g$, identifies $i$ with the base change of $\Delta_g$ along the map induced by $(f,f)$. Consequently $i$ is proper by step 2. The same step gives properness of $i\Delta_f$, since both factors are representable and proper. Hence $gf$ is separated.

source.place: Tag 050K (lemma-composition-separated), using the cartesian square in Tag 050H.

proof.text: Assume now that $f$ is representable by algebraic spaces. For the arbitrary test $(x_1,x_2,\alpha)$ of step 1 put $X_T=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}T$, where $T\to\mathcal B$ is $f(x_1)$. It is an algebraic space by representability. The two sections of $X_T\to T$ are $(x_1,\mathrm{id})$ and $(x_2,\alpha^{-1})$. Their equalizer sheaf is exactly the sheaf of $\beta:x_1\simeq x_2$ with $f(\beta)=\alpha$, by the arrow condition in a $2$-fibre product. Equivalently, the test $D_T\to T$ of $\Delta_f$ is the scheme-base change of the algebraic-space diagonal $X_T\to X_T\times_T X_T$ by this pair of sections. The algebraic-space diagonal scheme-test lemma says that this base change is a scheme and a monomorphism. Thus every scheme test of $\Delta_f$ is a scheme monomorphism. No etale atlas for $\mathcal A$ or $\mathcal B$ is needed.

If $f$ is separated, each $D_T\to T$ in step 5 is intrinsically proper as an algebraic-space map. It is representable by schemes since it is a scheme morphism. Apply the representable proper-test criterion and take its identity test $T\to T$ to obtain properness as a scheme morphism. Step 5 also gives a scheme monomorphism, so the proper-monomorphism criterion makes it a closed immersion. Conversely, suppose every scheme test of $\Delta_f$ is a closed immersion. Fix $T$ and any scheme map $T'\to T$. The scheme pullback $D_T\times_TT'\to T'$ is the test $D_{T'}\to T'$ of the same diagonal by the composite map from $T'$, hence is a closed immersion and therefore proper as a scheme morphism by clause (a) of the cited lemma. The representable proper-test criterion, now using all $T'\to T$, makes $D_T\to T$ intrinsically proper. All tests of $\Delta_f$ are proper, so $f$ is separated. This proves the asserted agreement with the closed-immersion diagonal predicate.
